nodes.name: CeOx NP synthesis with sonication
nodes.procedure: Synthesis of sub-10-nm CeO_x particles (4-10 nm, averaging 7.9±1.3 nm) with rough surface morphology. Sonication created transient (<1 ms) local high temperature (5000-5500 K via sonoluminescence) upon acoustic cavitation bubble collapse, eroding surface to expose high-energy facets. Carbon substrate used to facilitate dispersion of CeO_x.

unit_operations.name: Sonication
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Sonication created a transient (<1 ms) local high temperature (5000 to 5500 K, as indicated by sonoluminescence spectra; see fig. S1) upon the collapse of acoustic cavitation bubbles.

nodes.source_text: We applied a sonication-assisted polyol method to promote the growth of the high-energy facets by first synthesizing sub-10-nm CeO_x particles with rough surface morphology.

nodes.name: RIE sonication-assisted Ir/CeOx synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ir NPs nucleated onto sonication-prepared CeO_x support using sonication-assisted polyol method: iridium salt reduced to monodispersed Ir NPs in ethylene glycol with heating. Sonication triples CeO_x ripening rate via Ostwald ripening (small particles dissolve, recondense on larger ones). Ir nucleation completes in 1st hour, ripening continues; reaction extended to 3h for optimal embedding (~1nm depth). Carbon substrate removed by final air calcination. Final CeO_x size: 10.4±1.1 nm.

unit_operations.name: Polyol reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: iridium salt is reduced into monodispersed Ir NPs and loaded onto the metal oxide support by heating in ethylene glycol.

unit_operations.name: Sonication ripening
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: sonication was reintroduced during the Ir loading process, which was expected to expedite the dissolution of smaller particles and accelerate the ripening process. In this scenario, it was found that the ripening rate of the CeO_x support was tripled by sonication.

unit_operations.name: Calcination cleanup
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: carbon substrate was used to facilitate the dispersion of CeO_x which was removed at the end of synthesis by calcination in air.

nodes.source_text: Ir NPs were nucleated onto the prepared CeO_x support particles using the polyol method... sonication was reintroduced during the Ir loading process... reaction was prolonged to 3 hours to optimize the embedding process.

nodes.name: Control Ir loading on commercial CeO2
nodes.procedure: Ir NPs were nucleated onto ~30-nm commercial CeO2 crystallites using the same sonication-assisted polyol method for 3 hours.
nodes.source_text: Ir NPs were then nucleated onto these crystallites using the same sonication-assisted polyol method for 3 hours. The final product, namely C-Ir/CeO2.

nodes.description: PEMWE polarization curves - OER activity evaluation
nodes.source_text: Polarization curves verified the heightened OER activity of the catalyst, achieving a cell voltage of 1.72 V at a 3 A cm⁻² current density... accompanied by ∼99 and ∼98% Faraday efficiencies for H₂ and O₂ generation, respectively... mass activity of RIE-Ir/CeOₓ at 3 A cm⁻² was quantified at 777.4 A g_Ir⁻¹

The long-term stability... tested in an accelerated aging experiment that lasted for >6000 hours... with the current density stepped up from 1 A cm⁻² to 8 A cm⁻² and then reverted to 2 A cm⁻²... the decay rate at 3 A cm⁻² was evaluated to be 1.33 µV hour⁻¹
the control catalyst C - Ir / CeO₂ exhibited a much higher voltage decay rate of 3.1 mV hour⁻¹ during the 1 A cm⁻² to 8 A cm⁻² aging test
Chronopotentiometric curves of the PEMWE using RIE-Ir/CeOₓ... operated at 8 A cm⁻². TEM images... demonstrate the well-preserved embedding structure

nodes.characterization_summary: Cryo-TEM images of CeOx support show Ir NPs deposited after 5 min and more Ir NPs nucleated after 60 min of reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cryo-TEM revealed that a few Ir NPs were deposited on the roughened CeOx support after 5 min of reaction (Fig. 2B, dashed red circle; also in movie S2).

properties.description: Color TEM image showing nanostructure with purple, orange, and blue regions
Color TEM image with yellow and blue colored nanostructures

nodes.characterization_summary: Cryo-ET 3D models confirm Ir NPs not embedded after 5 min but embedded into CeOx support after 60 min to depth ~1.0 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At this initial stage, the cryo-ET image confirmed that the Ir NPs were not yet embedded into the CeOx support (Fig. 2F)... Notably, the Ir NPs were embedded into the CeOx support... reaching an embedding depth of ~1.0 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cs-corrected HAADF-STEM image shows embedding of Ir NPs into CeOx lattice to depth ~1 nm across crystallographic orientations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The final product, designated RIE-Ir/CeOx, was examined by spherical aberration-corrected scanning TEM... The high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) image (Fig. 2D) illustrates clearly the embedding of Ir NPs into the CeOx lattice to a depth of ~1 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images before/after 8 A cm^-2 OER test show preserved embedding structure in RIE-Ir/CeOx vs NP detachment/aggregation in C-Ir/CeO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images, taken before and after the 8 Acm−2 constant current density test, clearly demonstrate the well-preserved embedding structure in RIE-Ir/CeOx, contrasting starkly with the evident NP detachment and aggregation in C-Ir/CeO2 (Fig. 3B, insets...)

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes and nanoparticle morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows broad peaks for sub-10 nm CeOx particles consistent with particle size 7.9±1.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The size of the as-synthesized CeOx NPs ranged from 4 to 10 nm averaging 7.9±1.3 nm (Fig. 2A and fig. S2), in line with the broad peaks in the x-ray diffraction spectrum (see figs. S6 to S8 for detailed characterizations).

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller method determines surface areas of RIE-Ir/CeOx, C-Ir/CeO2, and commercial IrO2 for specific activity normalization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After normalization with surface areas determined by the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller method or electrochemical active surface area, the specific activity of RIE-Ir/CeOx maintained its superiority over both C-Ir/CeO2 and commercial IrO2 (figs. S45 to S47).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms Ir content of 15.6 wt% in RIE-Ir/CeOx and 17.2 wt% in C-Ir/CeO2; validates inhibition of Ir dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: considering its lower Ir content (15.6 wt %; table S9)... C-Ir/CeO2 (17.2 wt %)... Inhibition of Ir dissolution and detachment in RIE-Ir/CeOx was further validated by ICP-MS measurements...
